observations: Photo 0 shows the retail box for a Blue Gate Line Interactive UPS.
The model 'BG1230 Elite Pro' is clearly printed on the box in photo 0.
The box is secured with white plastic shipping straps.
The actual UPS unit is not visible in the photo.
The background shows a wall-mounted fan and a television, suggesting a retail or warehouse environment.

claims.evidence: The model number BG1230 on the box in photo 0 corresponds to the 1230VA rating.
Internal battery specifications cannot be confirmed without opening the unit or seeing the technical plate on the device itself.

risks.risk: The box may be empty or contain a different, older, or damaged unit.
risks.proof: A photo of the actual UPS unit outside of the box showing the rear identification label.
risks.if_unproven: as a scam risk or empty box

risks.risk: The internal lead-acid batteries may be depleted or dead from long-term storage or use.
risks.proof: A video showing the UPS powering a load (e.g., a lamp) while the input power cord is unplugged.

risks.risk: The charging or inverter circuitry may be faulty.
risks.proof: A video of the unit successfully completing a self-test upon power-up.

proof_requests: Photo of the actual UPS unit removed from the box.
Photo of the manufacturer's label on the back of the UPS unit.
Video of the UPS unit turned on and powering a device while disconnected from the wall outlet.
response.reason: The seller has only provided a photo of the retail packaging. Without seeing the actual item, its presence, physical condition, and functional state cannot be assessed even for a worst-case valuation.
